items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: The name of the band that I played with, Doug, is funny. It was called Fishers Ragtime Military Jazz Band.

ctx.x: Did they call it jazz then?

Yes. The name of the band that I played with, Doug, is funny. It was called Fishers Ragtime Military Jazz Band. Fishers? My father, my father was a drummer, bass drummer in the band. In those days, they used two drums. My father was the bass drummer, and a fellow by the name of Rag Baby Stevens was the snare drummer. And my father built a harness for me so that I could carry the snare drum. And we made this Rex Parade, which was the big carnival parade even then. And Fishers Band was the only band in the parade…
E-flat clarinet's pretty well disappeared these days.

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: You see, like I tell you, I had a card here of Fisher's Band where it was printed on it, Fisher's Ragtime Military Jazz Band. Now that's, when I first played, I was eight years old, that first job, the first parade I ever played.

ctx.x: And you don't remember the ear of the word jazz?

No, no. If I said so, I'd be lying, Dick. I don't. This all of a sudden there it was. But even before, you know, I was a kid. But even before, I can go back this far, but even before they ever had jazz bands at all, ragtime bands or whatever you want to call them. You see, like I tell you, I had a card here of Fisher's Band where it was printed on it, Fisher's Ragtime Military Jazz Band. Now that's, when I first played, I was eight years old, that first job, the first parade I ever played. Now if I was born in…
This Fisher card. They used to call it Swing. This Fisher card, they'll call it Ragtime, not Jazz. Is that right? Huh? The Fisher, you mentioned Fisher.
